messages:
emily: Hey team, customer reports service endpoint `acme-api.svc.redwood.internal` started returning NXDOMAIN from their pods this morning after a hosted zone rename on their account. They say external calls to the same endpoint still resolve fine. Can someone triage?
kevin: @emily do we have the customer account ID and VPC?
emily: yes — acct 987654321, VPC vpc-0a1b2c3d (us-west-2). Customer says problem started ~08:10 PDT.
maria: quick guess: split-horizon/private hosted zone shadowing or VPC association change. Ask for `dig` from pod and from the node-local resolver.
emily: asked customer for dig output; they pasted this from a pod:
```
; <<>> DiG 9.16.1 <<>> acme-api.svc.redwood.internal @127.0.0.53
;; global options: +cmd
;; ->>HEADER<<- opcode: QUERY, status: NXDOMAIN, id: 12345
;; flags: qr rd ra; QUERY: 1, ANSWER: 0, AUTHORITY: 1, ADDITIONAL: 1
;; AUTHORITY SECTION:
acme-api.svc.redwood.internal. 300 IN SOA ns-123.awsdns-45.net. hostmaster.amazon.com. 1 7200 900 1209600 300
```
kevin: from the node (host) dig shows SERVFAIL for the same name? ask for that.
emily: they sent host dig too:
```
; <<>> DiG 9.16.1 <<>> acme-api.svc.redwood.internal @169.254.169.253
;; ->>HEADER<<- opcode: QUERY, status: SERVFAIL, id: 54321
```
maria: SERVFAIL from the VPC resolver + NXDOMAIN from pod usually means node-local cache/nodelocaldns or kube-dns is getting a negative answer cached from a different resolver. Could be overlapping private hosted zones in a different account or a resolver rule forwarding to a stale forwarder.
kevin: run `aws route53 list-hosted-zones-by-name --dns-name "svc.redwood.internal"` in the customer's account — check for duplicate private hosted zones and VPC associations. Also `aws ec2 describe-vpcs --vpc-ids vpc-0a1b2c3d` to confirm account/VPC.
emily: customer ran the checks and pasted results (redacted):
```
HOSTED ZONES FOUND:
- HostedZoneId: ZONEAAAAA  Name: svc.redwood.internal  PrivateZone: true  VPCs: [vpc-0a1b2c3d] (account 987654321)
- HostedZoneId: ZONEBBBBB  Name: svc.redwood.internal  PrivateZone: true  VPCs: [vpc-0f9e8d7c] (account 123456789)
```
maria: aha — two private hosted zones with same name in different accounts. If VPCs are peered or resolver rules forward across accounts, that can cause unpredictable resolution depending on priority. Also if the other zone had a rename or record deletion earlier, negative caching might have propagated.
kevin: do they have a Route53 outbound/inbound resolver rule or a conditional forwarder? Ask for `aws route53resolver list-resolver-rules` and `list-resolver-rule-associations` in both accounts.
emily: customer checked and found a resolver rule in acct 123456789 that forwards `svc.redwood.internal` to a contrived forwarder IP (10.10.10.2) — it was created during a migration. That forwarder returned NXDOMAIN for the service for a window while records were moved. Negative TTL is 300s.
maria: that explains the pod NXDOMAIN. Node-local saw NXDOMAIN cached, and pods continued to get NXDOMAIN until TTL expired. To fix: either remove the resolver rule or change its priority so the VPC's own private hosted zone wins, and disassociate the peered VPC from the conflicting private hosted zone.
emily: customer asks for minimal steps to unblock quickly.
kevin: immediate mitigation: 1) flush node-local DNS cache on nodes (restart `kube-dns` or `nodelocaldns` DaemonSet) 2) temporarily remove or disable the conditional forwarder in acct 123456789 so the VPC resolver doesn't get NXDOMAIN from the forwarder. After cache flush, test again.
maria: CI-friendly commands they can run:
```
# restart nodelocaldns daemonset
kubectl -n kube-system rollout restart daemonset/nodelocaldns
# or restart kube-dns
kubectl -n kube-system rollout restart deployment/coredns
```
emily: customer applied both: removed resolver rule in the other account and restarted nodelocaldns. They report intermittent success — some pods still see NXDOMAIN.
maria: that's expected until negative TTLs expire and caches propagate. Check pod `/etc/resolv.conf` to ensure they point to `127.0.0.53`/node-local; confirm no stale sidecar overriding DNS.
emily: customer confirmed pods use node-local. They ran `dig` again from a failing pod and now see an answer: A record 10.2.3.4.
```
; <<>> DiG 9.16.1 <<>> acme-api.svc.redwood.internal @127.0.0.53
;; ->>HEADER<<- opcode: QUERY, status: NOERROR, id: 67890
;; ANSWER SECTION:
acme-api.svc.redwood.internal. 60 IN A 10.2.3.4
```
kevin: great. For long-term: 1) avoid duplicate private hosted zones (use cross-account hosted zone management or centralize), 2) if conditional forwarding is required, set resolver rule priority carefully and document ownership, 3) lower negative caching TTLs during migrations.
maria: also consider adding a Route53 health-check or automation to detect when a forwarder returns NXDOMAIN for expected records.
emily: filing an internal postmortem for the customer — notes: root cause = conditional forwarder in account 123456789 returning NXDOMAIN during hosted-zone rename; negative caching + node-local DNS caused pods to continue seeing NXDOMAIN until TTL expiry. Remediation = removed rule, flushed caches, confirmed resolution. Next steps: coordinate a cleanup to disassociate peered VPC from ZONEBBBBB or rename to avoid collision.
deploy-bot: [change] applied by kevin — removed resolver rule (rr-0xabc) in acct 123456789 at 2024-11-06T15:23:07Z :white_check_mark:
emily: thanks all — customer confirmed full recovery and will schedule a DNS cleanup with infra team. :tada:
